research_question: Owned-page scope: Smokeball Legal Software and Automatic Time Capture. Planned sources and method: Smokeball official documentation; test a disclosed billing workflow. Build a source-labelled comparison covering Smokeball time tracking and Smokeball billing; record dates, definitions and sample limits. Sources are proposed, not verified findings.

research_brief.purpose: Explain how Smokeball AutoTime turns tracked activity into time entries, which plans include it, when it creates no entry, and how a firm can test whether captured time becomes approved, invoiced, and collected fees.
research_brief.audience: Managing partners, billing managers, and operations leads at small and midsize firms evaluating Smokeball or its AutoTime feature.
research_brief.data_period: Smokeball pricing page and Support Hub articles as displayed on October 3, 2026
research_brief.scope_limitations: Desk research from public Smokeball pages; no quote requested, no hands-on test, and no pilot run. Smokeball publishes no prices, so none are stated or estimated. The 10% to 30% figure is a vendor claim with no published method. The pilot measures and review steps are an editorial framework, not Smokeball guidance.

claims.statement: Smokeball publishes no plan prices; AutoTime is included with Prosper+ and is an add-on for Grow, while Bill, Boost, and Grow list manual time tracking.

AutoTime creates time entries nightly from tracked activity, is configured per user, lists nine no-entry situations, logs one minute per 10-second-plus view in New Outlook, and does not bill entries automatically.

Smokeball supports manual time tracking, a timer, activity codes, and Time Finder; integrates with QuickBooks Online; does not handle payroll or general ledger; and exports activity and time data to CSV.
